mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in a month
failure_condition: Over a 36-month rolling window, 20-day forward returns during FEDFUNDS > 4% events are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) using a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement raises perceived risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% and remains above for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Elevated unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: During such labor disengagement regimes, 60-day forward returns are not systematically negative (p > 0.05) relative to a control window of similar macro conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private demand) exceeds INDPRO by more than 10% for two consecutive months, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be positive as excess demand supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO > 0.10 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Economic expansion with strong demand relative to production
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in 70% of such triggered windows, controlling for FEDFUNDS and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 5% for three consecutive months predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as it signals contracting supply capacity and potential valuation compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by at least 5% each month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During such supply contractions, 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (mean <= 0 with p > 0.05) relative to a neutral supply growth baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS falls below 2% for four consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, the S&P 500 exhibits positive 20-day forward returns as lower policy rates lower discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.0% for four consecutive months and UNRATE < 4.0%
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during such episodes when compared to a neutral policy rate path using IV regression controls.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (labor market activity) below 120,000 in a month coincides with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market participants interpret weakness as a risk-on signal for safe-haven flows.
failure_condition: During such events, 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) after adjusting for contemporaneous moves in VIX and GOOG.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (retail sales) exceeds CPIAUCSL by more than 8% for two consecutive months in a non-inflationary context, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be positive as it signals robust consumer demand supporting equities.
candidate_trigger: HOUST - CPIAUCSL > 0.08 for two consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 210
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during such demand surges are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) after controlling for FEDFUNDS and M2 growth.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-side shock where RSAFS ( inventories) rises by more than 15% in a month while INDPRO remains flat is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as excess inventory accumulation depresses market valuations.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >15% in a month and INDPRO remains unchanged for that month
regime_hint: Inventory accumulation shock (not offset by production growth)
failure_condition: During such inventory spikes, 20-day forward returns are not systematically negative (mean <= 0 with p > 0.05) after accounting for FEDFUNDS and S&P 500 volatility changes.
